text: Lionel Messi broke the all-time World Cup scoring record — a hat-trick against Algeria and a brace against Austria put him on five goals and top of the Golden Boot race.
Cristiano Ronaldo scored twice as Portugal beat Uzbekistan 5-0 — becoming the first player ever to score in SIX different World Cups.
Erling Haaland is on four World Cup goals, two in each of Norway's opening games — and faces Mbappé's France in a Golden Boot showdown on June 26.
Kylian Mbappé struck a double for France at the World Cup — also on four goals — in a match delayed nearly two hours by adverse weather. Allez les Bleus.
Vinícius Júnior scored in all three World Cup group games — only the fifth Brazilian ever to do it, joining Ronaldo, Romário, Rivaldo and Jairzinho.
